subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Protostars: The First Glow
description: A fast breakdown of Protostars: The First Glow for builders.

hook.text: Before becoming a true star, a collapsing gas cloud spends millions of years as a protostar—hot but not yet fusing.

buildup.text: As gravity compresses the core, temperatures climb. The protostar glows in infrared, hidden inside dust.

discovery.text: When the core reaches 10 million °C, hydrogen nuclei fuse into helium. Nuclear fusion ignites—a star is born.

twist.text: Not every protostar makes it. Objects below 0.08 solar masses never get hot enough—they become brown dwarfs.

climax.text: The newborn star blows away remaining dust with radiation pressure, revealing itself to the universe.

punchline.text: Millions of years of collapse. Then fusion ignites in an instant.

quiz.question: What happens if a protostar doesn't reach 10 million °C at its core?
options: It becomes a brown dwarf—too cool for hydrogen fusion
It collapses directly into a black hole

details.summary: A protostar forms when a collapsing cloud core heats up from gravitational compression but hasn't yet reached temperatures for hydrogen fusion. This phase lasts tens of thousands to millions of years, during which the protostar is hidden inside a cocoon of gas and dust, visible only in infrared…
details.whyItMatters: Protostars represent the critical transition between cold gas clouds and true stars. Understanding this phase reveals how quickly stars form and how planetary systems begin taking shape in surrounding debris disks.
takeaways: Protostars heat from gravitational compression, not fusion
They're hidden in dust cocoons visible only in infrared
This phase lasts thousands to millions of years

faq.question: When does a protostar become a true star?
faq.answer: When its core temperature reaches about 10 million degrees Celsius and hydrogen fusion begins. This moment marks the transition from a protostar to a main-sequence star. For sun-like stars, this takes roughly 50 million years from initial cloud collapse.

faq.question: What happens to the gas and dust around a protostar?
faq.answer: It flattens into a rotating accretion disk. Some material falls onto the protostar, increasing its mass. The remaining disk can form planets, asteroids, and comets — making every protostellar disk a potential solar system in the making.
